Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Long COVID patients with vitamin D deficiency had higher depressive symptom scores than those without deficiency.
Sentence: "Moreover, patients in the VDD group had significantly higher scores for physical and mental fatigue as well as higher scores for depressive symptoms."
Measured as: depressive symptom scores
Population: Outpatients with long COVID infected during the Omicron phase (n=97)
Intervention: Vitamin D deficiency (serum 25-OHD below 20 ng/mL), observed not assigned
Comparator: Non-deficient vitamin D group (25-OHD at or above 20 ng/mL)
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 97
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Vitamin D supplementation did not change depressive symptoms (HAMD-17) compared with control in patients with low vitamin D.
Sentence: "The HAMD-17, RSAS, and RPAS scores did not change significantly between VD and control groups from baseline to endpoint (all p > .05)."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (HAMD-17)
Population: Patients with depression and anxiety with low serum 25(OH)D levels
Intervention: Daily vitamin D supplementation for 6 months
Comparator: Control group
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Responses
